businessType.title:
Tell Us About
Your Business
businessType.subtitle: Your business type and size determine your CIT rate, VAT filing duties, and e-invoice timeline. This only takes a moment.
businessType.turnoverHint: Used to determine your VAT filing status and e-invoice phase. You can update this later.
businessType.whyBody: Nigerian tax law ties your CIT rate, VAT filing exemptions, and e-invoicing deadline directly to your business type and turnover. Getting this right means fewer surprises and accurate guidance.

descriptions.sole_trader: Best for one-person businesses and freelancers with personal tax obligations.
descriptions.partnership: For shared ownership businesses where partners split profits and reporting duties.
descriptions.limited_company: For registered companies that need company tax guidance and annual filing support.
descriptions.ngo: For missions, associations, and non-profits that still need a clean compliance record.

tinVerify.title: Verify Your TIN
tinVerify.body: Your Tax Identification Number goes on every invoice you issue. It's how NRS links your business to its tax records.
tinVerify.formatHint: Usually 8–14 digits. Find it on your NRS certificate or old FIRS documents.
tinVerify.nrsNote: Managed by NRS (Nigeria Revenue Service, formerly FIRS)
tinVerify.pendingNote: Verification takes 1–2 minutes via NRS. We'll notify you automatically when it's confirmed.
tinVerify.whtWarningTitle: Without a TIN, you lose 10% on every payment
tinVerify.whtWarningBody: Clients are legally required to withhold 10% WHT from payments to businesses without a valid TIN. That money is very difficult to recover.
tinVerify.educationBody: A valid TIN reduces payment friction, protects you from avoidable withholding tax, and makes invoices easier for clients to approve. It's the single most important step for your tax health.

vatSetup.title: VAT Setup
vatSetup.exemptTitle: You're exempt from filing VAT returns
vatSetup.exemptBody: Businesses under ₦100M turnover are exempt from filing VAT returns. But here's the important part — you must still charge 7.5% VAT on all invoices.
vatSetup.exemptDetail: Your annual turnover is below the ₦100M threshold, so you don't need to submit monthly VAT returns to NRS. TaxBridge will remind you if your turnover changes.
vatSetup.requiredTitle: You must file VAT returns monthly
vatSetup.requiredBody: Your turnover exceeds ₦100M, so VAT returns are due by the 21st of each month.
vatSetup.requiredDetail: Late filing attracts penalties. TaxBridge will send you reminders before each deadline and help you calculate the amounts.
vatSetup.rate: Standard rate on goods and services
vatSetup.distinctionTitle: Two things to know about VAT
vatSetup.chargingBody: Every Nigerian business must add 7.5% VAT to invoices for taxable goods and services. TaxBridge does this automatically.
vatSetup.filingExemptBody: You're currently exempt from filing returns because your turnover is under ₦100M. This can change if your business grows.
vatSetup.filingRequiredBody: You must file by the 21st of each month. TaxBridge will remind you and help calculate the amount due.
vatSetup.educationBody: Every invoice you create in TaxBridge automatically includes the correct 7.5% VAT line. If filing is required, we'll prepare your return summary with one tap.

einvoice.title: E-Invoicing
einvoice.phaseSmall: E-invoicing becomes mandatory for your business size from July 2027. Getting set up early gives you a head start with banks and larger clients.
einvoice.phaseMedium: The pilot phase is active now. E-invoicing becomes mandatory for your business size on July 1, 2026. We recommend applying for FIRSMBS integration.
einvoice.phaseLarge: E-invoicing enforcement is active for businesses your size. Non-compliance carries a ₦200,000 penalty plus 100% of tax due.
einvoice.enforcementBody: Businesses with ₦5B+ turnover must issue compliant e-invoices. Penalties include ₦200,000 per offence and 100% of the tax due on uninvoiced transactions.

large.label: Large companies (₦5B+)
large.desc: Enforcement active since April 2026. Full compliance required.

small.label: Small & micro businesses
small.desc: Voluntary until July 2027. Early adoption earns better trust scores.

einvoice.platform: E-invoices are submitted via FIRSMBS (NRS Merchant-Buyer Solution). TaxBridge connects to this platform on your behalf.
einvoice.educationBody: Businesses that adopt e-invoicing early get faster loan approvals, smoother audits, and higher trust scores with larger clients and banks. TaxBridge makes it easy to get ready.
